questions.text: Consider a message signal [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})[/latex] which is bandlimited to [latex][-\mathrm{W}, \mathrm{W}][/latex], where W is in Hz . Consider the following two modulation schemes for the message signal: Double sideband-suppressed carrier (DSB-SC): [latex]f_{D S B}(t)=A_{c} m(t) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)[/latex] Amplitude modulation (AM): [latex]f_{A M}(t)=A_{c}(1+\mu m(t)) \cos \left(2 \pi f_{c} t\right)[/latex] Here, [latex]A_{c}[/latex] and [latex]f_{c}[/latex] are the amplitude and frequency (in Hz ) of the carrier, respectively. In the case of AM, [latex]\mu[/latex] denotes the modulation index. Consider the following statements: (i) An envelope detector can be used for demodulation in the DSB-SC scheme if [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})>0[/latex] for all t . (ii) An envelope detector can be used for demodulation in the AM scheme only if [latex]\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{t})>0[/latex] for all t . Which of the following options is/are correct?

questions.text: Consider a continuous-time finite-energy signal [latex]f(t)[/latex] whose Fourier transform vanishes outside the frequency interval [latex]\left[-\omega_{c}, \omega_{c}\right][/latex], where [latex]\omega_{c}[/latex] is in rad/sec. The signal [latex]f(t)[/latex] is uniformly sampled to obtain [latex]y(t)=f(t) p(t)[/latex]. questions.text: A source transmits symbol [latex]S[/latex] that takes values uniformly at random from the set [latex]\{-2,0,2\}[/latex]. The receiver obtains [latex]Y=S+N[/latex], where [latex]N[/latex] is a zero-mean Gaussian random variable independent of [latex]S[/latex]. Suppose the probability of symbol estimation error [latex]\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{e}}[/latex] is expressed as follows: [latex]\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{e}}=\alpha \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{N}>1)[/latex], where [latex]\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{N}>1)[/latex] denotes the probability that [latex]N[/latex] exceeds 1. What is the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] ?

(ii) The autocorrelation function [latex]\mathrm{E}[\mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}) \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{t}+\tau)][/latex] is independent of time t for all [latex]\tau[/latex].
